rows.text: The Assembly's item created at 17:23 on Thursday 19 July 2012 states that the Fale Alea has recommended ('KUO fokotu'u 'e he Fale Alea 'o Tonga') Lord Fakafanua to become the Speaker ('Eiki Sea) and Tu'iha'ateiho for the post of Deputy Speaker ('Lakanga Tokoni Sea'), and quotes the Legislative Assembly Act ('kupu 16') that the King appoints the Speaker from the nobles' representatives on the Assembly's recommendation, to hold office under clause 61 of the Constitution.
rows.uncertainty: The Assembly's recommendation, not the royal appointment. The statute is cited as section ('kupu') 16, whereas MIC's English release cites clause 15 and Act 21 of 2010 makes section 15 the Speaker provision; kept as printed. The English rendering is this packet's reading.

rows.text: The same item ends: 'Koe fakanofo 'oku toki fakahoko ia 'e he 'Ene 'Afio Tupou VI koe Tu'i 'o e 'Otu Tonga' (the appointment is then made by His Majesty Tupou VI, King of Tonga).
rows.uncertainty: Read as prospective: 'toki' marks the appointment as following the recommendation. It shows that at 17:23 on 19 July the appointment had not been reported, which is in tension with the Assembly's later statement that he was appointed on 19 July (to_fakafanua_royal_appointment_20120719); both can be true only if the appointment followed later that day. The sentence names nobody.
